name: Mawson's Huts
funding: Conserved by the Mawson's Huts Foundation with the Australian Antarctic Division. It told Treasury it had raised over A$9M in cash and kind, A$2.5M of it federal grants; its Hobart replica museum also pays.
watch: Its chair, Greg Holland, formerly chaired Alcohol Beverages Australia; a director, Greg Carter, works for expedition cruise operator Antarpply Expeditions.
records_note: A registered charity (ABN 78 077 696 649); its site lists its board and staff, and its 2017-18 pre-budget submission to Treasury set out expedition costs.
operator: Mawson's Huts Foundation and Australian Antarctic Division

name: Antarctic Artists and Writers Program (Polar STEAM)
funding: US National Science Foundation gives logistics and flights, not cash. Since 2022 Oregon State University runs it under Polar STEAM, a US$4M NSF cooperative agreement to 2028.
watch: NSF lists the old standalone solicitation as archived; the programme now depends on one agreement ending in August 2028.
records_note: NSF publishes the award, its yearly obligations and past participants; the pin marks McMurdo, one of three US year-round stations.
operator: US National Science Foundation; Oregon State University

name: Port Lockroy (Base A, Bransfield House)
funding: Run by the UK Antarctic Heritage Trust, which took £1.65M in the year to April 2025: £927,850 from its shops and £715,974 from donations, membership and grants. HX and Quark are listed supporters.
watch: Sales in the shop and post office to cruise passengers pay for the site, which takes up to 18,000 visitors a season.
records_note: The Trust files accounts with the Charity Commission (no. 1160847); its 2024-25 report names its patron, trustees, major partners and supporters.

name: Scott's Discovery Hut
funding: Antarctic Heritage Trust (NZ charity CC24071) took NZ$3.43M in the year to June 2025, NZ$1.54M of it government grants; its partners page names MFAT, the Ministry for Culture and Heritage and ANZ as core funders.
watch: The hut stands 300m from the US McMurdo station; visitors arriving there or at Scott Base are likely to encounter it.
records_note: The Trust files audited annual returns with New Zealand's Charities Register; its partners page shows funders as logos, with no amounts.

name: Scott's Hut, Cape Evans (Terra Nova Hut)
funding: Conserved by New Zealand's Antarctic Heritage Trust (NZ$3.43M income in 2024-25, NZ$1.54M from government). In 2007 the British Government gave £250,000 towards restoring Scott's huts.
watch: Heritage Expeditions, the Trust's expedition partner, sails to the Ross Sea huts and donates part of the fare of supporters who book with it.
records_note: The Trust files audited annual returns with New Zealand's Charities Register and sells the hut's conservation plan on request.

name: Shackleton's Hut, Cape Royds (Nimrod Hut)
funding: Antarctic Heritage Trust (NZ charity CC24071) took NZ$3.43M in the year to June 2025, NZ$1.54M of it government grants; its partners page names MFAT, the Ministry for Culture and Heritage and ANZ as core funders.
watch: The Shackleton whisky brand is a listed key supporter of the Trust, which conserved the hut and its 6,000 artefacts.
records_note: The Trust files audited annual returns with New Zealand's Charities Register and sells the hut's conservation plan on request.

name: Holy Trinity Church
funding: Built with donations collected across Russia by the charity Temple for Antarctica, approved by Patriarch Alexius II; priests from the Trinity Lavra of St Sergius staff it year round.
watch: Patriarch Kirill, who held a service here in 2016, has been under UK sanctions since June 2022 for supporting Russia's war on Ukraine.
why_flagged: The head of the church that staffs it, Patriarch Kirill, is under UK sanctions since 16 June 2022.
records_note: No accounts or donor list found for the church or for the Temple for Antarctica charity.
operator: Russian Orthodox Church (Trinity Lavra of St Sergius)

name: Wordie House (Base F)
funding: Managed since 2014 by the UK Antarctic Heritage Trust, a charity paid for mainly by its shop sales, donations, membership and grants; staff of Ukraine's Vernadsky station help keep the hut.
watch: The Trust's least visited site, it can still receive more than 2,000 visitors a year.
records_note: Covered by the Trust's accounts filed with the Charity Commission (no. 1160847); no figures are given for this hut alone.

name: Military Trophy Park
funding: Azerbaijani state project. President Ilham Aliyev ordered it built in January 2021 and opened it on 12 April 2021, according to the presidential website.
watch: The Council of Europe human rights commissioner, the European Parliament and Armenia objected. Wax figures and helmets left the main display in October 2021.

propaganda.summary: President Ilham Aliyev proposed and opened the park, and his website says it shows the victory and Armenian war crimes. Until October 2021 it displayed wax figures of Armenian soldiers.

name: Bangabandhu Memorial Museum
funding: The Bangabandhu Memorial Trust ran it from 1994; banks gave it 1,360 million taka in 2017 and Standard Bank 100 million in 2020. The Yunus government revoked its tax exemption.
watch: The house where Mujib was killed in 1975, with a six-storey extension from 2011; burned on 5 August 2024 and demolished in February 2025.

propaganda.summary: Sheikh Hasina's trust opened the museum in her father's house in 1994; as prime minister she held state salutes and party ceremonies there each August. Protesters burned it in 2024 and razed it in 2025.
